subject: Unexpected rejection of initial values with truncated posterior

messages.author: b0e39a5c5669abe3
messages.subject: Unexpected rejection of initial values with truncated posterior
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to infer the location and scale of a truncated normal distribution, but I'm having trouble altering the location parameter's constraints. Here's my Stan code—which seems to work—given that my data are real values that fall within [0, U]:

data {
    int<lower=1> U;  // value bound.
    int<lower=1> N;  // observation count.
    vector<lower=0, upper=U>[N] X;  // observed values.
}
parameters {
    real mu;
    real<lower=0> sigma;
}
model {
    // Likelihood.
    for (n in 1:N) {
        X[n] ~ normal(mu, sigma) T[0, U];
    }

    // Prior.
    mu ~ normal(0, 1000);
    sigma ~ normal(0, 1000);  // behaves as if T[0,].
}

I get a reasonable-looking distribution over mu. However, I wanted to see what the posterior would look like if I restricted mu to the range [0, U]:

parameters {
    real<lower=0, upper=U> mu;
    real<lower=0> sigma;
}

Now, every time I run the program I just get the errors

Rejecting initial value:
    Gradient evaluated at the initial value is not finite.
    Stan can't start sampling from this initial value.

Initialization between (-2, 2) failed after 100 attempts. 
   Try specifying initial values, reducing ranges of constrained values, or reparameterizing the model. 

Am I missing something? It seems to me that the default initial values will fall within [0, U], and that the posterior is well defined there, so I can't figure out why the sampling fails.

Some other things worth mentioning:
  • Everything seems to work fine when the upper bound U is removed from mu's constraints, i.e., real<lower=0> mu. However, if I negate all of the data (so they lie in [-U, 0]), and update the constraints on X and the likelihood function accordingly, then I can't get the program to work—even with no constraints on mu.
  • I've tried setting init=0, so that the unconstrained initial value is always 0, but I get the same errors. I've been using seed=4, if that helps.
  • I've tried replacing the likelihood loop with vectorised calls to normal_lpdf, log_diff_exp, and normal_ldf, as explained on page 294 of the (Python) Stan manual, but I get the same error.
The data: U=3600, and X=[943.98, 60.82, 2069.22, 1141.29, 301.57, 1351.71, 477.01, 464.02, 535.58, 528.77, 1520.36, 3435.04, 1579.43, 1674.24, 744.56, 815.46, 887.49].

Thanks,
Kevin

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Unexpected rejection of initial values with truncated posterior
parts:
What happens when you set the bounds (0, U) on mu is that random
initialization is centered around U / 2; more specifically, it's
U * inv_logit(uniform(-2, 2)).

When you have the bounds (0, infinity) on sigma, the initialization
is centered around 1; more specifically, random inits will be
exp(uniform(-2, 2)).

When you put those together, you're trying to evaluate
the gradient of the log density, it underflows due to double-precision
arithmetic.

If you take the same model and provide reasonable inits, such
as mu=1500 and sigma=1500, it will fit OK with that data:

mean se_mean sd 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% n_eff Rhat
mu 520 13 310 39 295 486 725 1173 536 1
sigma 1267 17 321 814 1041 1211 1414 2094 363 1

In general, putting things on a more unit-like scale will help immensely
with Stan's adaptation, as well as its ability to get off the ground.

- Bob
